paragraphs.text: "They are my bulwark against the Terror. They are the Defenders of Humanity. They are my Space Marines." —The Emperor of Mankind
paragraphs.card: And They Shall Know No Fear

paragraphs.text: They all took up the cry, the missionaries, the pilgrims, the sisters of the Orders Militant. The forces of Chaos melted before the fire of their faith.
"Our will shall be our weapons, our faith shall be our armour." —Canticle of Absolution
Through blood and battle, scouts are forged from raw recruits into the Imperium's finest.
The practice of tracking and training Thunderwolves is a sort of initiation ritual into the upper echelons of the Wolf Guard.
There is no greater bulwark than the Praetors of the Adeptus Custodes, the bodyguards of the Emperor of Mankind.
Harrowing visions, paralyzing pain, and terrifying brain spasms await those who challenge the cult.
The Lords of Change are Tzeentch's greatest servants. The most powerful of them wield fragments of his power over destiny.
"Though it may take an eternity, I will see the myriad dynasties united once more."
Blight grenades—which induce horrendous effects on their victims—have no impact on the Death Guard, who gladly use the devices in extreme close quarters with the enemy.
There are those who draw false comparisons between the tech-magi of the Adeptus Mechanicus and the xenotechnologists of the necron race. There can be no mercy for such heretics.
Those suspected of carrying the flayer curse are summarily banished, lest the corruption spread to other Necrons.
"Immortality is not quite the same as invulnerability, but it is close enough."
"Only the deathless can truly comprehend the burden of unfailing loyalty." —Vargard Obyron of the Sautekh Dynasty
"I am the Arch-fiend, the Despoiler of Worlds, and by my hands shall the false Emperor fall." —Abaddon the Despoiler
"This galaxy once knelt before us, and it will do so again."
"In the embrace of the great Nurgle, I am no longer afraid, for with His pestilential favour I have become that which I once most feared: Death." —Kulvain Hestarius of the Death Guard
Each plaguebearer is formed from the blighted soul of a mortal slain by Nurgle's Rot.
High-ranking plaguebearers of Nurgle's realm ride into realspace mounted upon Rot Flies—colossal daemonic insects whose appearance is so repugnant it scars the mind.
Masters of dimensional dissonance, singularity manipulation, and countless other technologies, plasmancers are terrifying to behold.
Poxwalkers are victims of the Walking Pox, a cruel virulence which rots the infected to death while keeping them conscious.
"Embrace the strength of your Primarch, but deny the Red Thirst, brothers! There is no return from that darkest of paths."
"Nothing clears a battlefield like a Deathstrike missile. Wait. Is something moving out there?" —Commander Zander At'lan, Tallarn 115th Armoured Regiment
"Aza'gorod, the Nightbringer. The embodiment of death. A killer of stars and of worlds." —Illuminor Szeras
Nothing can override the hard-wired desire to kill that empowers these rage-driven Necrons.
"Witchcraft or technology, it is blasphemous, and it must be stopped." —Inquisitor Greyfax
"When the Silent King saw what had been done, he knew at last the true nature of the C'tan, and the doom they had wrought in his name." —*The Book of Mournful Night*
The Archaeovist of the Solemnace Galleries will not rest until every treasure in the galaxy is safely within his clutches.
"Scour this world of these impudent trespassers!" —Lord Traedrekkh of the Sekemtar Dynasty
Too obviously xenos in form to blend into human society, the acolytes haunt the dark places beneath industrial sprawls.
The Brazen Thunder, foremost of the bloodcrusher legions, are named for the sound they make as they ride into battle.
"Charge brothers! Death to the false Emperor!"
"I can show you indulgence without regret, delight without boundaries, gratifications beyond count." —Sha'ris, Deacon of Lust
To look upon one is to surrender every last shred of self-will.
Its shriek is unintelligible, but armored bulkheads seem to understand the intent well enough.
War is a dance. And they're looking for partners.
"We guarantee you that within a week, you will feel like a new man." —Galaxos Klynesmith, biophagus
Charged with psychic energy, the melee weapons of the Tyranid are far more than bone and chitin.
"The star-born approach! Their holy angels descend! Take up arms, my brothers and sisters, for the Day of Ascension is upon us!"
The blessed union of gun, claw, and merciless intent is a force to be truly feared.
It emits a stinking cloud composed of millions of nascent microscopic organisms, each possessing a fragment of predatory sentience.
By the time the Blood Angels descended from the heavens, Phodia was a city transformed. Miles of flesh-filled rivers fed into the central digestion pools and up into the hive fleet above.
A foe without honour is a foe already beaten.
Skulls for the Skull Throne.
"Engaging Protector protocol."
Created to break will and bone with equal ferocity.
"This heresy cannot stand!"
"Bolters? Chainswords? All fine weapons, however I wield a far more dangerous power."
"Some may question your right to destroy ten billion people. Those who understand know that you have no right to let them live." —Exterminatus Extremis
They dive screaming on defensive lines, sowing chaos before the main assault begins.
"No. No! Not the sarcophagus . . . Khorne damn you, you disloyal curs. JUST KILL ME!" —Kalos the Ravager
The gods of Chaos bestow gifts of mutations upon their champions. Too many of these gifts transform their bearer into mindless, writhing chaos spawn.
Every kill is a sacrament of the Emperor's glory.
The astropath collapsed, his empty eye sockets aglow. He spoke three words before falling lifeless to the ground: "They . . . are . . . coming!"
"Ours is to honour the martyr, tend the fallen, defend the innocent, and walk always in the light." —*The Hospitaller's Book of Hours*
"I shall seek the Emperor's forgiveness in the darkest places of the night." —Oath of the Penitent
"I shall seek the Emperor's forgiveness in the darkest places of the night." —Oath the Penitent
The walls of the Necron tomb were unbreakable. The ground beneath it was not.
Tzeentch's beastmen twist reality as they themselves are twisted.
"See that cloud that hangs around it? More than a minute in there and you'll be bleeding out of places you didn't even know you had." —Captain Ascote
A hive tyrant's synaptic link is the primary conduit through which the Hive Mind enforces its dominance over a hive fleet's lesser creatures.
Bound to a cryptek, the cryptothrall exists for one reason: to defend its master to the death.
It burns with the very fire that doomed Szarekh's species, and channels it to devastate his foes.
Under his rule, there is but one creed: Chaos shall reign.
"By this oath, I pledge to stand by thee, against traitor, beast, or fiend, for only in death does duty end."
"When the door drops, give them a taste of the Emperor's fire!" —Commissar Yarrick
"Now!"
The battle began with an overwhelming wave of Tyranids and ended with Canoness Lucretia standing atop a huge pile of charred alien corpses.
The Battle of Baal was the bloodiest and most costly in the entire noble history of the Sons of Sanguinius.
"It is their duty to fight and die so that Humanity might be preserved." —Lord Commissar Barron Reed
"Hunger is no different from any other foe; defeat it in the Emperor's name, and save Humanity." —Motto of the Agri-World Viridia IV
No berzerker charge can stand against the psychic might of the Hive Mind.
The Changer of Ways often sends glimpses of possible futures to his most loyal acolytes, visions that would destroy lesser minds.
"We've reached the xenos HQ. Transmitting coordinates now."
"Rise and serve me once more." —Trazyn the Infinite

"Hold your bitterness deep within, and there let it fester. Let it roil and squirm and churn, until you are filled with bile so poisonous that all you touch falls to ruin." —Mortarion, Daemon Primarch
"Hold your bitterness deep within, and there let it fester. Let it roil and squirm and churn, until you are filled with bile so poisonous that all you touch falls to ruin." —Morarion, Daemon Primarch
"Praise Nurgle! For the plague to have progressed so quickly, truly his blessing must be upon us!" —Ku'gath Plaguefather
By the physical laws of our universe, darkness is merely the absence of light. Necrons can harness the power of other dimensions, where darkness is tangible and moldable.
"Agresto, bring up the rear . . . Agresto?" —Sergeant Dremark Eigen, last words
"Bolters, flamers, plasma—we hit the xenos with everything, and it just kept coming." —Captain Uriel Ventris
"Pray that night is upon us, for if this twilight is the work of the Necrons, we are all dead men." —Address by Lieutenant Krakos prior to the Bloodmoon Massacres
"Pray that night is upon us, for if this twilight is the work of the Necrons, we are all dead men." —Address by Lieutenant Krakow prior to the Bloodmoon Massacres
"You mortals turn to dust in the blink of an eye. I only expedite your fate."
In the roiling depths of the Eye of Terror, the bloodthirsty hordes of Chaos Marines plot the downfall of their loyalist brethren.
"Tzeentch cares not what they were or what they become. Only that they change." —Kairos Fateweaver
"That which was, will be. That which will be, was." —Kairos Fateweaver
"They're beasts! What are they going to do, bomb us from orbit?" —Platoon Commander Cyrus Jalili, Prandium Defence Auxilia
"They're beasts! What are they going to do, bomb us from orbit?" —Platoon Commander Cyrus Jalili, Prandium Defense Auxilia
Khorne's sole desire is to drown the galaxy in a tide of slaughter. To conquer and kill every living thing, until there is nothing left but spilled blood and shattered bone.
A single spore from a Tyranid Hive Ship can spell doom for a solar system.
The Genestealer Cults rejoiced at the arrival of their gods . . . at first.
The Tyranids advance inexorably across the galaxy in their living Hive Ships, with one singular goal: to consume all.
The Tyranids advanced inexorably across the galaxy in their living Hive Ships, with one singular goal: to consume all.
"Once we have claimed this planet, we will claim the stars."
As the fusillade of lasgun fire bounced harmlessly off the carnifex's carapace, the creature roared and advanced.
With each defeat, the hive learns. With each victory, it grows.
The voice of a clamavus commands all who carry the genetic legacy of the Tyranids in their blood.
Tyranids flourish in any climate, dominate any ecosystem, crush any resistance.
Upon impact with a planet's surface, a tyrannocyte's bloated belly bursts open, disgorging a horde of Tyranid invaders.
Upon impact with a planet's surface, a tyranocyte's bloated belly bursts open, disgorging a horde of Tyranid invaders.
"Looks like we've found the source. Torch it quick, before anything crawls out." —Sergeant "Ripper" Jackson
At the lash of the hive ship's feeder tentacles, the cruiser vented atmosphere, cargo, and crew members into the void.
"This sword has many names. You may call it 'Death.'" —Kaldor Draigo, Supreme Grand Master of the Grey Knights
"Target eradicated. That which burns shall ever be blessed." —Fusilave unit Tor-213
"Target eradicated. That which burns shall never be blessed." —Fusilave unit Tor-213
Countless xenos cults dwell unseen within the Imperium, lurking just beneath the surface.
All Necrons bear the mark of the Triarch, a brand upon their living-metal skin that binds them to their dynasty.
As part of their indoctrination and training, a psyker learns to focus their mental strength through a psycho-reactive staff.
Used carefully, material that has been exposed to the baleful energies of the Warp can be contained to fuel powerful rituals.
Used carefully, material has been exposed to the baleful energies of the Warp can be contained to fuel powerful rituals.
"This cogitator provides a strategic overview of the battlefield. By which I mean, of course, the entire planet."
Within it rests the power of a sun, and none of the warmth.
The arcane sphere that hovers near Magnus's staff imbues it with the power to transform enemies into mindless chaos spawn.
The flesh of the Necrontyr is a memory so distant as to be nearly mythical.
"While we slept, our inferiors infested the worlds that belong to us. Now, we awaken once more." —Szarekh, the Silent King
"The ancient Necron race has achieved this pinnacle of elegance through their relentless pursuit of utility." —Tech-Priest Darvin, executed for heresy 1256998.M41
The vaults of the Necron Dynasties contain all manner of esoteric artifacts, most forged long before many of the younger races even existed.
"Pain is an ally. Pain is a friend. Pain is truth." —Sister Erynica N'botu, Order of the Valorous Heart
"Pain is an ally. Pain is a friend. Pain is truth." —Sister Erynia N'botu, Order of the Valorous Heart
During biotransference, the Necrontyr lost almost all individuality. What little remained was imprisoned within a living metal form.
Necrodermis, the living metal from which all Necrons are made, is endlessly adaptive.
Only the most pious and devoted Imperial servants are granted the posthumous honor of becoming servo-skulls.
"One day, the dark glory of the void will swallow the light of the stars once and for all!" —Magus Lucea Kane
"As Horus once besieged the Sol System, we shall bring the rotting Imperium to its knees." —Abaddon the Despoiler
"Of all the stars in the Galaxy, Sol is of the Emperor. Its heat is His might. Its light is His revelation." —*Lectitio Divinitatus*
"Once, the C'tan sought to rule us. Now it is they who serve us, their shards powering our great machines." —Szarekh, the Silent King
"It is my cry that wakes you in the night, and my body that crouches in the shadow. I am Tzeentch and you are the puppet that dances to my tune." —*The Book of Tzeentch*
"As swift as a lash mamba, as sharp as a spineleaf, as stubborn as a wild grox." —Colonel Pannet, in praise of the Catachan warrior
"As swift as a lash mamba, as sharp as a spineleaf, a stubborn as a wild grox." —Colonel Pannet, in praise of the Catachan warrior
"My Master is the Beginning and he is the End. He is the Master of Mortals, and the core of our Dead Hearts." —*The Saga of Khorne*
"We shall wage this war with undaunted faith and courage. We shall not take one step back." —Lord Marshal Toshenko to the Vostroyan 16th
"Embrace your hunger, your lust, your desire. The universe is ours for the taking!" —Sanctifer LeVay, Cult of the Sacred Union
"Any Cadian who can't field-strip their own lasgun by age ten was born on the wrong planet." —Anonymous
Before the Great Sleep, the Necrons knew every corner of the galaxy, as only the ultimate conquerors could.
"It's a lifeless ruin of some long-lost race. What is there to fear?" —Commissar Gadholm
When Chaos makes a tool that isn't specifically for destroying things, it's usually for finding new things to destroy.
Anrakyr the Traveller awoke from his slumber with a singular goal: to rebuild a united Necron galaxy.
Anrakyr the Traveler awoke from his slumber with a singular goal: to rebuild a united Necron galaxy.
"Power comes in many shapes. But real power does the shaping." —Abaddon the Despoiler
The Emperor is the greatest psyker in Human history. For thousands of years, he has sat immobile in a palace that spans a continent.
Deserts of industrial ash surround the hive cities, covering the surface of the planet with an unstable, corrosive skin.
Millennia of constant warfare have left many planets with very little worth fighting over.
Centuries' worth of black iron lie beneath the soil of every Imperial world, their civilization built on never-ending strife.
All orbital bombardment did was till the soil.
In the late stages of a Tyranid invasion, vast capillary towers funnel biomass to the Hive Ships waiting in orbit.
On the Planet of Sorcerers in the Eye of Terror lies the Tower of the Cyclops, the redoubt of Magnus the Red.
"The war will be decided here, where the planet's defences are strongest." —Marneus Calgar
The squad plunged deep into Hive Pandorial, finding only the shambling corpses of those they came to avenge.
The Chapter's honored dead are interred in the Hall of Heroes, where the mineral-rich water of the catacombs slowly fossilizes their bones, preserving them for all time.
On countless frontier worlds, below silica sand, blasted chalk, or bubbling marsh, slumbering Necrons wait.
On countless frontier worlds, below silica sand, blasted chalk, or bubbling marsh, slumbering Necrons await.
Armageddon has become a site of holy pilgrimage for the Orks: a planet where the fighting never stops.
"What are ramparts, what are steeples, what are our machines worth in the teeth of this ceaseless hunger?" —Magos Varnak
In the late stages of a Tyranid invasion, sessile organisms take root in a planet's crust, converting its resources into biomass that can be extracted by the Hive Fleet.
When the Great Rift opened across the Galaxy, many Imperial worlds were lost to Chaos.
When the Great Rift opened across the galaxy, many Imperial worlds were lost to chaos.
In the hearts of mortals, in the pages of ancient lore, in the deep, forgotten places of the universe . . . Chaos waits.
In the hearts of mortals, in the pages of ancient lore, in the deep, forgotten places of the universe . . . Chaos awaits.
Disillusioned with the Imperium, the population of Chancer's Vale turned to other, hungrier powers for meaning.
"It appears Old One Eye is on the hunt." —Marneus Calgar
As the continent sank over the course of eons, the tomb complex slowly flooded. The sleeping Necrons, their stasis crypts corrupted, never awoke.
The Imperium's most peaceful worlds serve only to arm and supply the others.
Stripped and blasted by millennia of war, every planet eventually looks the same.
"Let the others bicker over their little worlds and stars. I have an empire of knowledge, and it encompasses all others." —Trazyn the Infinite
Defence laser emplacements are usually located at high altitude, where the rarified air does little to impede their range of destructive efficacy.
Defense laser emplacements are usually located at high altitude, where the rarified air does little to impede their range of destructive efficacy.
The weapons deployed to drive the Traitor Legions into the Eye of Terror were so destructive that some planets still have not recovered.
Most denizens of an Imperial hive city live and die without ever setting foot inside the towering skyscrapers of the ruling class.
Most denizens of the Imperial hive city live and die without ever setting foot inside the towering skyscrapers of the ruling class.
Abandoned tunnels and bunkers below the hive city have been secretly recolonized and dubbed the "Forbidden Cities."
In its attempts to mirror Tzeentch's convoluted scheming, the Crystal Labyrinth constantly shifts and rearranges itself.
Places of worship become frenzies of violence as the psychic call of the Hive Mind stirs Genestealer Cults to action.
"Hail the Children of the Stars!" —Magus Lucea Kane
Genestealer Cults bide their time on Imperial worlds, spreading tendrils of corruption through the native population.
Chaos renegades always seek to deface and destroy effigies of Imperial piety, replacing them with blasphemous symbols of the Ruinous Powers.
The Cicatrix Maledictum split the galaxy asunder. The raw stuff of Chaos flooded into realspace, transforming whole planets in moments.
Mere weeks later, the planet was scoured of any trace of life. Every scrap of vegetation, every drop of water—gone.
Deep-space ports provide temporary shelter for Imperial cruisers on long voyages.
Heretic cultists came to the planet Sovereign in search of resources and precious artifacts. They found something else.
Heretic cultures came to planet Sovereign in search of resources and precious artifacts. They found something else.
